finding: The live range of $90-$750 is about right, but it is wide because it joins two different jobs: a cleaning (roughly $70-$230) and a replacement (roughly $320-$710 on the vehicles checked). Showing them as two ranges would be clearer. Built replacement totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2020 Jeep Compass 2.4L about $319-$705 (0.6-1.0 hr); midsize 2018 Chevrolet Malibu 1.5L up to about $361 (0.2-0.8 hr; no aftermarket price found, so no low total; with the genuine part at a discount price of $114 it is about $138); truck 2018 Ford F-150 5.0L up to about $706 (0.5-1.0 hr; about $387 with the genuine part at a discount price of $327); luxury 2011 Cadillac CTS 3.6L up to about $517 (0.6-0.8 hr; about $288 with the genuine part at a discount price of $216). Cleaning only: a mechanic-written consumer guide (Jerry) gives 0.5-0.8 hr for a typical cleaning and 0.8-1.2 hr when the throttle body is removed for a deep clean, which is $60-$192 of labor at $120-$160/hr, plus about $10-$40 for cleaner and a gasket: roughly $70-$230. A relearn with a scan tool adds 0.2-0.4 hr ($24-$64) per the same guide; an Acura bulletin prints 0.2 hr for 'Reset the throttle position value and idle learn procedure'. One GM bulletin allows 1.2 hr for remove, clean, replace the sensor cover, relearn and diagnosis together. So the $90 floor fits a cleaning (lowest benchmark $90), and nothing found supports a replacement that cheap. The $750 top fits the mainstream cases but can be exceeded: RepairPal's average is $623-$766, YourMechanic shows $807-$1,204 at a shop or dealer for a 2017 F-150 3.5L turbo, and a 2024-2025 Jeep Wrangler 2.0L turbo bulletin allows 2.7 hr for the throttle body alone ($324-$432 of labor before parts). How solid the labor times are: all four classes have a manufacturer-stated time for the example vehicle (Compass 0.6 hr, Malibu 0.2 hr, F-150 0.5 hr, CTS 0.8 hr), but these are warranty times, the low end of what shops bill, and the Malibu's 0.2 hr sits beside charge-air-tube work and looks optimistic as a stand-alone job. The high ends are an older-Malibu GM time and a general 50-60 minute figure from a consumer guide, not vehicle-specific. Parts are the weak side: an aftermarket price was confirmed only for the Compass, the CTS has a single priced source, and the luxury example is an older domestic car; no European luxury throttle body was priced, and those can cost more. Our totals sit below RepairPal mainly because its parts figure ($492-$573) is higher than the list prices found for the Malibu and CTS.
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis or scan fee, a new throttle body gasket (about $18 list on the Compass), shop supplies and tax. Many shops try a cleaning first: about 0.5-1.2 hr of labor plus cleaner, roughly $70-$230. After either a cleaning or a replacement, most drive-by-wire cars need an idle/throttle relearn, which some shops include and others bill at about 0.2-0.4 hr. An air filter, intake tube or clamp, or a wiring connector repair may be quoted at the same time. An estimate is not a quote and not a diagnosis: the same warning light or reduced-power message can come from wiring, the pedal sensor or a vacuum leak.
